newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures closed at their lows on Friday after a seesaw day, finally driven lower by position unwinding ahead of a long U.S. weekend.

"It wasn't really profit-taking. If it had been, we would have gone lower," one trader said. "It's just that since people have been long for a long time, they have a wide profit margin and they are lightening up after the sharp rise at the beginning of the week."
Another trader said the correction of the last two sessions was healthy and the notionnel was established in a range between 126.18 and 126.80, which should set the stage for further gains.
Dealers said the notionnel could break out above 126.80 on market-friendly U.S. CPI numbers due on Wednesday.
Bond futures, franc and PIBOR futures were hit in late morning with another rumour, categorically denied, of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's resignation.

The franc which started out around 3.3807 per mark, fell as low as 3.3873 per mark as the rumour made its way through the markets. Once the denial was issued, the franc climbed off its lows to trade at about 3.3840 per mark late in the day.
Market-friendly U.S. data lifted futures sharply in the afternoon but the rise was erased by position unwinding later.
U.S. retail sales rose 0.7 percent in September, much higher than expected, but the rise was offset by a sharp downward revision to August figures and subdued producer price data.
Some traders said they expected the notionnel to break through 127 in the days ahead.
But others said the franc and French markets generally could come under pressure next week as a series of strikes unfolds during the week.
